excerpt: A practical due-diligence checklist for overseas buyers assessing UAE ownership, contracts, payments, financing and remote management.
introduction:
An overseas buyer can organise much of a UAE property search remotely, but the title, buyer eligibility, seller authority, payment destination and actual condition of the unit still need independent checks. Processes differ by emirate and by property.

Build a document trail before transferring funds, and appoint qualified local professionals where needed.
takeaways: Confirm the exact registered right and buyer eligibility with the relevant authority.
Verify the agent, project, seller and payment recipient independently.
Plan financing, inspection, management and the eventual exit before signing.

sections.heading: Identify the property and right
sections.body:
Obtain the emirate, community, building, unit number and current registration document. Confirm whether the right offered is freehold or another registered interest and whether the buyer's nationality or entity is eligible for that precise unit. The [UAE government's ownership overview](https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/moving-to-the-uae/expatriates-buying-a-property-in-the-uae) explains that rules differ by emirate.

Ask the competent authority to verify the current position; do not rely on a marketing statement that all foreign buyers can own everywhere. Review the seller's identity and authority, any mortgage or tenancy and required clearances. A reservation receipt does not itself transfer a registered right.

sections.heading: Verify the people involved
sections.body:
Request the agent's professional registration and the brokerage licence, then check them with the responsible local regulator. [Dubai Land Department's licensed broker service](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/licensed-real-estate-brokers/?r=1) is a Dubai example; other emirates have their own procedures. Confirm that the person and company match the listing and that the seller authorised the marketing.

Agree the scope, commission, payment trigger and any exclusivity in writing. If appointing a lawyer, inspector or manager, confirm their qualifications, fees and duties separately. Check the agent’s licence alongside the property’s title and condition.

sections.heading: Inspect beyond the photographs
sections.body:
Arrange a live viewing or independent inspection of the actual apartment, building and parking. Compare the floor plan, dimensions, view, fixtures and condition with the contractual description. Ask about cooling, plumbing, visible moisture and maintenance history. For an off-plan home, inspect the site where possible and review the approved specification and construction evidence.

Request the current service-charge statement, building rules and planned work. Ask whether advertised facilities and beach access are operating or still planned. Compare the actual property and its documented rights with the show unit and marketing material.

sections.heading: Understand every payment
sections.body:
Obtain an itemised purchase budget including price, authority charges, brokerage, inspection, lender fees and initial work. Independently verify the beneficiary and account through official channels. For off-plan purchases, ask the authority how to verify the project's approved payment arrangement. Keep receipts and do not count a deposit credited to price twice.

A sample AED 1,000,000 purchase with AED 60,000 in acquisition and initial costs requires AED 1,060,000 before a separate reserve. Use the example to prepare a clear purchase budget and a separate ownership reserve. Exchange-rate conversion and bank transfer costs may affect an overseas buyer's total.

sections.heading: Prepare for remote signing
sections.body:
Ask the local authority and your legal adviser what identity, attestation, translation or power-of-attorney documents are required for the chosen transaction. The requirements depend on where documents are issued and how they will be used. Allow time for verification and never assume a generic document is accepted everywhere.

Define any representative's powers narrowly, including the property, permitted actions, payment authority and expiry. Verify the representative independently. Review the signed sale agreement, payment dates, conditions, deposit treatment and remedies before instructing a transfer.

sections.heading: Arrange finance and reserves
sections.body:
Non-resident lending policies vary by bank and property. Request a written offer, valuation, fees, insurance and repayment schedule; approval in principle may remain subject to conditions. If the valuation is lower than the purchase price, the required cash contribution can increase.

Keep a reserve for delayed completion, vacancies, repairs and currency fluctuations. For off-plan, map all instalments against reliable funds rather than relying on a future resale. For ready property, check any existing tenancy and the process for transferring deposits and utilities.

sections.heading: Plan ownership after completion
sections.body:
Decide who will hold keys, inspect the property, market it, collect rent and approve maintenance. Obtain a written management agreement showing fees, reporting frequency, repair limits, insurance, deposit handling and termination. Verify whether the intended rental use requires a local permit or building approval.

Use recent comparable leases where available and deduct vacancy, service charges and owner costs. Estimate a sale using comparable completed transactions, expected selling expenses and any loan settlement. Neither a marketed yield nor a planned development guarantees a return.

sections.heading: Coordinate the handover from abroad
sections.body:
Before completing, agree who will attend the inspection, receive keys, open utility accounts and check that outstanding charges have been settled. Ask your representative to provide dated photographs, a meter reading and a written record of any defect. Confirm the scope of any authority you grant and how it can be revoked or allowed to expire.

For an existing tenant, obtain the current lease and establish how the deposit, prepaid rent and notice communications will be handled at transfer. For a new unit, request warranties, appliance manuals and management contacts. Keep a digital copy of the registration record, sale agreement and receipts in a secure location. Ask a local adviser to explain any document that differs from the original contract before signing acceptance.

sections.heading: Request current documents
sections.body:
Use the [RAK area guide](/journal/ras-al-khaimah-property-lifestyle) or [Ajman area guide](/journal/ajman-property-2026) for location context, then browse [Aliyas UAE projects](/projects). [Contact Aliyas](/contact) with your nationality, budget and intended use and ask for current unit documentation.

Confirm the right, fees, payment process and professional credentials independently before signing or transferring funds.
